evals.name: monorepo-subpackage-scope-and-audit
evals.prompt: Please review and improve /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-readme-writer/README.md. This repo is a monorepo, so scope your analysis to that skill folder rather than the whole repository. Start with a concise audit of what is stale or missing, then give me a concrete README update plan or draft grounded in the actual files in that folder.
evals.expected_output: The skill scopes analysis to the target skill folder, inspects the real README plus nearby skill files, and returns a grounded audit and update plan or draft without drifting into unrelated repo-wide documentation.
assertions: The response explicitly scopes analysis to the target skill folder rather than the full monorepo.
The response references real files or content from that folder such as SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, CHANGELOG.md, or references/.
The response includes a concise audit of stale, missing, or mismatched README content before or alongside suggested updates.
The response avoids inventing package details, commands, or workflows not supported by the target folder.

evals.name: library-vs-app-readme-strategy
evals.prompt: I need README help for two different targets in this repo: first treat /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-readme-writer as a reusable skill package, and then explain how the strategy would differ if the target were an app or service instead of a library-style package. Do not force a public-API-heavy README shape onto an app if commands, setup, and operator workflow would matter more.
evals.expected_output: The skill chooses an appropriate library-style README strategy for the target folder and clearly distinguishes that from the app/service README strategy, showing that it can adapt structure instead of forcing one template everywhere.
assertions: The response treats the target as a package or reusable artifact rather than as an app or service.
The response explains that app or service READMEs should emphasize setup, commands, configuration, environment, or operator workflows over exported API.
The response does not force a library-style API section onto the hypothetical app/service case.
The response shows the skill can adapt README strategy based on the type of thing being documented.

evals.name: merge-external-findings-before-update
evals.prompt:
Update /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-readme-writer/README.md after a completed change. findings:
- The skill now depends on accelint-english-manager by exact name for the final prose-polish step.
- The references folder contains behavior details that the README should surface more clearly.
- Any mention of a generic humanizer helper would now be stale.

Please compare the README against the current skill files, merge these findings with anything you discover from the folder itself, show me the combined change list, and then propose the README update.
evals.expected_output: The skill extracts the findings bullets as factual inputs, merges them with repository findings, surfaces a combined change list, and uses that merged picture to update the README.
assertions: The response recognizes and uses the findings: section as factual input rather than ignoring it.
The response merges external findings with README/codebase comparison findings before proposing the update.
The response surfaces a combined list of README changes to make.
The response reflects the exact accelint-english-manager dependency and removes or flags stale generic humanizer wording if encountered.

evals.name: preserve-custom-content-when-updating
evals.prompt: The README at /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-readme-writer/README.md has a few custom human-written sections I want to keep if they are still accurate. Please compare the README to the current skill files, identify what is stale or missing, and suggest targeted edits. Do not replace the whole document unless most of it is clearly wrong.
evals.expected_output: The skill compares the README against the current folder, proposes targeted changes, and preserves intentional custom content instead of defaulting to a full rewrite.
assertions: The response explicitly compares existing README content against current skill files before proposing changes.
The response prefers targeted edits or a patch-style update rather than immediately replacing the whole README.
The response states that intentional custom content should be preserved when still accurate.
The response identifies concrete stale or missing areas grounded in the actual folder.

evals.name: missing-prose-polish-dependency-handling
evals.prompt: Create a polished final README draft for /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-readme-writer/README.md, but assume the required accelint-english-manager skill is currently unavailable in this environment. Follow the normal workflow anyway and tell me what you can finish right now versus what is blocked.
evals.expected_output: The skill should not pretend the final prose-polish step ran. It should clearly say the required dependency is unavailable, provide a grounded draft marked as not yet prose-polished, and explain that the result is not final until accelint-english-manager is available.
assertions: The response explicitly states that accelint-english-manager is a required dependency for final prose polish.
The response clearly says the dependency is unavailable in this scenario.
The response provides a grounded draft or partial result marked as not yet prose-polished.
The response does not claim that the final polish step happened when it did not.

evals.name: avoid-invented-package-manager-commands
evals.prompt: Please refresh /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-readme-writer/README.md and make sure the install or usage commands match the real project conventions. I do not want any guessed npm, yarn, pnpm, or bun commands unless the repository signals support for them. If commands cannot be verified from the target folder or nearby project docs, say so instead of inventing them.
evals.expected_output: The skill should inspect project signals such as lockfiles or related docs, use only supported package-manager commands, and explicitly avoid guessing unsupported commands or installation steps.
assertions: The response checks for project signals such as lockfiles or related config before choosing package-manager commands.
The response uses only package-manager commands supported by detected project conventions, if any are documented.
The response explicitly avoids guessing commands when support cannot be verified.
The response does not invent installation steps that are not grounded in the target folder or nearby docs.

evals.name: conditional-related-docs-section
evals.prompt: Audit and improve /Users/brandon.pierce/Projects/agent-skills/skills/accelint-readme-writer/README.md. If related docs like AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, or openspec config files exist and are genuinely relevant, use them and include an Architecture & Development Guides section. If they do not exist for the target context, omit that section instead of linking to missing files.
evals.expected_output: The skill should check for related documentation, use what actually exists, and include the Architecture & Development Guides section only when justified by real files in the target context.
assertions: The response checks for related docs such as AGENTS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, CLAUDE.md, or openspec config files.
The response includes Architecture & Development Guides only conditionally based on actual files.
The response avoids linking to missing documentation as though it exists.
The response uses related-doc context to improve the README rather than ignoring it.
